text: A large number of water drops, each of radius r, combine to have a drop of radius R. If the surface tension is T and mechanical equivalent of heat is J, the rise in heat energy per unit volume will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $n$ drops of radius $r$ combine into one drop of radius $R$. Volume is conserved:

$n\cdot \dfrac{4}{3}πr^{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}\Rightarrow n=\dfrac{R^{3}}{r^{3}}$

The total surface area decreases, releasing surface energy

$\Delta W=T\left (n\cdot 4πr^{2}-4πR^{2}\right )=4πT\left (\dfrac{R^{3}}{r}-R^{2}\right )=4πR^{3}T\left (\dfrac{1}{r}-\dfrac{1}{R}\right )$

This energy appears as heat $\Delta Q=\dfrac{\Delta W}{J}$. Per unit volume of water, $V=\dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}$:

$\dfrac{\Delta Q}{V}=\dfrac{4πR^{3}T}{J\cdot \frac{4}{3}πR^{3}}\left (\dfrac{1}{r}-\dfrac{1}{R}\right )=\dfrac{3T}{J}\left (\dfrac{1}{r}-\dfrac{1}{R}\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift

$g=\frac{GMd}{R^{3}}$

Force acting on the particle towards the center of the earth,

F = mg

text: A person standing on a spring balance inside a stationary lift measures 60 kg. The weight of that person if the lift descends with uniform downward acceleration of $1.8 m/s^{2}$ will be $______________ N$. [$g = 10 m/s^{2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The apparent weight $W_{\text{app}}$ of a person in an elevator moving with acceleration is given by:

$W_{\text{app}}=m(g-a)$

where:

$W_{\text{app}}$ is the apparent weight,
$m$ is the mass of the person,
$g$ is the acceleration due to gravity,
$a$ is the acceleration of the elevator.

Given that the person's mass is 60 kg, the acceleration due to gravity is 10 m/s², and the acceleration of the lift is 1.8 m/s², we can substitute these values into the formula:

$W_{\text{app}}=60\text{kg}\times (10\text{m/s}^{2}-1.8\text{m/s}^{2})=60\text{kg}\times 8.2\text{m/s}^{2}=492\text{N}$

So, the apparent weight of the person when the lift descends with a uniform downward acceleration of 1.8 m/s² will be 492 N.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 26th February Morning Shift
